core_obligations: Part (1): deduce from the discussion of changing topologies on ringed sites that pulling back the sheaf associated to a quasi-coherent module on S gives the sheaf associated to the pulled back module (proof lines 3138-3139).

Part (2): explain why the compatibility with pushforward cannot even be stated -- pushforward need not preserve quasi-coherent modules -- and why any formulation over the big sites would force pushforward to commute with arbitrary base change (proof lines 3140-3145).

Part (2), counterexample: take the quasi-compact open immersion of the punctured plane into the plane over a field, note that the pushforward of the structure sheaf of the source is the structure sheaf of the target, and observe that after base change along the zero section the pushforward becomes zero (proof lines 3146-3150).

Part (3): record that f and its base changes preserve quasi-coherent modules, then rewrite the asserted equality of sheaves as the equality of the two spaces of sections over an etale morphism into S, namely sections of the pullback of the pushforward against sections of the pullback of the original sheaf over the fibre product (proof lines 3153-3160).
Part (3), conclusion: obtain that equality from flat base change for cohomology of coherent sheaves (proof lines 3160-3161).
proof_roadmap: Part (1) from the change-of-topology remark (proof lines 3138-3139).
Part (2) as a warning, with the reason no precise statement exists (proof lines 3140-3145).
Part (2) as an explicit counterexample, the punctured plane over a field (proof lines 3146-3150).
Part (3): reduce the equality of sheaves to an equality of sections over an etale morphism (proof lines 3153-3160).
Part (3): conclude by flat base change (proof lines 3160-3161).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of schemes f : T to S the proposition has three parts: the equivalences of categories identifying quasi-coherent modules on S with those on the big and small sites are compatible with pullback, in the sense that pulling back the sheaf associated to a quasi-coherent module is the sheaf associated to the pulled back module; the corresponding compatibility with pushforward fails, and not even the statement can be made precise in general; and when f is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the topology is Zariski or etale, pushforward of quasi-coherent modules along f and along the induced morphism of small sites stays quasi-coherent and the square comparing pushforward with the association F to F^a commutes (statement lines 3108-3135). The claim is H3 for two reasons. First, part (2) is carried by an explicit counterexample, the quasi-compact open immersion of the punctured plane into the plane, where the pushforward of the structure sheaf of the punctured plane is the structure sheaf of the plane but becomes zero after base change to the origin; the author also explains why no precise statement is available, namely that compatibility over the big sites would force pushforward to commute with arbitrary base change (proof lines 3140-3150). Second, part (3) is a separate argument that turns the asserted equality of sheaves into a statement about sections over an etale morphism into S and identifies the two sides by flat base change (proof lines 3153-3161). What keeps this below a routine derivation is precisely that a counterexample has to be exhibited for one part and a flat base change identification carried out for another.
